- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to correct; apply downward bias starting from day of sentiment change.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 10-day mean, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 70% of 30-day moving average, model often overreacted; apply downward correction proportional to sentiment decay.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.50” values, model tends to ignore sentiment; force a small upward bias (e.g., +0.5–1.0) to counteract underestimation.
